cases.C16: Imprimatur Labs turns permission into a product promise: governed agents act only with sanction. Ecclesiastical associations are real, but clear registration and multiple domains support a distinctive, serious identity.
cases.C26: Chary is rare enough to trademark and own outright—unlike Shield or Guardian. One-hearing lesson fixes 'charity' misreads; CISOs respect a word that means exactly what it does.
cases.C25: Runnymede's constitutional resonance makes constrained authority instantly legible to British enterprise buyers. 'Labs' clearly separates it from the charity and council, creating a distinct, highly credible, registrable brand.
cases.C18: For UK CISOs unconcerned with niche American subcultures, 'Redoubt' is a sober military-engineering term that perfectly captures an architecture of fortified containment, standing clear of tired shield-and-guard AI clichés.
cases.C29: Seneschal Labs: archaic precision signals a steward acting only under strict grant—exactly governed AI. Companies House and .labs domains are clear; no major clash; memorable despite slight spelling effort.
cases.C14: Vouchsafe Labs stresses granted permission, not blind trust—agents receive access deliberately. Companies House and .labs domains are clear; existing identity-verification startups are adjacent, not an AI/security software conflict.
cases.C27: Chosen enclosure, not isolation: the anchorite's cell is governance made visible—AI limited to granted bounds, human authority outside. Clear UK name, free domains, no active AI clash.
cases.C12: Veto names the exact human-approval control; clarity beats crowding. UK company clear and vetolabs.co.uk/.ai/.io free. In regulated sales, plain veto is instantly understood.
cases.C22: Bailiwick means one's rightful jurisdiction — precisely the bounded authority an architecture of distrust requires. Offshore finance is one association among many; IT namesake sits in a separate sector.
cases.C11: Latin 'cautio' means a legal bond — fitting for AI trust. The dashcam Cautio sits in fleet video, a separate market; spelling divergence protects against confusion. 'Cautious' resonance aids recall.
cases.C23: Perfect metaphor for 'architecture of distrust': a penstock meters flow under pressure — exactly what the platform does with AI capabilities. 'Labs' signals R&D depth, distinguishes from healthcare SaaS (Penstock Group) and pentesting (Pentera). Industrial
cases.C24: Claustra evokes a concrete, weighty gate—exactly the 'information only where allowed' principle. Latin lends gravitas for C‑level audiences; the claustrophobia link is niche and can be reframed as controlled access.
cases.C17: Seneschor (seneschal) instantly conveys entrusted authority without sovereign power, mirroring revocable AI permissions. Its medieval roots sound prestigious yet distinct, and the name is unclaimed in the AI‑security arena.
cases.C30: The institutional tone provides the sobriety CISOs demand. 'Provost' perfectly encapsulates delegated authority and oversight, while 'Labs' balances this with technical agility and innovation.
cases.C15: Countermand captures the core promise: human veto over risky AI. Military feel suits regulated sectors valuing command discipline. Verb-forward naming (like Darktrace) aids recall. Ownership clean, domains strong.
cases.C31: Vallum's rampart metaphor perfectly embodies architecture of distrust: bounded, controlled, sovereign. Roman resonance adds gravitas for enterprise buyers. Vallum.ai's governance focus is adjacent, not direct competition; positioning as infrastructure, not governance tool, differentiates cleanly.
